experiment.experiment: Targeted search fallback, not a random recall benchmark or full batch run
experiment.selection: Three previously unresolved companies with 9, 10 and 40 registered employees

scope: Read-only review of saved pilot envelope, attempt records, request receipts and fetched snapshots. No live API calls, no key access, no source changes.

results.name: VADS? M?BELSENTER AS
results.diagnosis: Returned nominees were third-party/wrong-owner destinations. Varanger KraftMarked page is a utility-company site; its exact-name hit is a customer feature (?Vads? M?belsenter AS er ?rets siste m?nedens kunde?), not ownership evidence. Its contact/about pages identify Varanger KraftMarked. Largestcompanies is a general directory homepage (.com) with no target legal proof. Regnskapstall is a directory profile whose detail subpage reproduces the exact target legal name, org no. 930 969 095 and Tanavegen 4 / 9801 Vads?, but this is third-party registry data, not evidence the target owns that domain; saved info/contact pages identify Regnskapstall as a Digitale Medier 1881 / Opplysningen 1881 service. Gate outcomes correctly remain ambiguous. No official_website claim or exact target-owner proof was missed in saved pages.

describes Varanger KraftMarked as the power supplier

results.name: LILLESTR?M PIZZADRIFT AS
results.diagnosis: No usable candidate URL was emitted, fetched, or gate-assessed. Saved official workplace is PIZZABAKEREN LILLESTR?M (10 employees) with no website or business email field. The pilot intentionally did not preserve raw search results/query text, so cannot distinguish zero web results from all results excluded by nomination filters; no evidence of a missed proof or gate false negative.

results.name: M?LLER SPORTSBILER ASKER & B?RUM AS
results.diagnosis: No new usable search candidate URL was emitted, fetched, or gate-assessed; raw results were not retained. The baseline frozen run already had official workplace candidate porsche-asker.no, whose robots.txt fetch returned HTTP 429, a servicefactory.no workplace-brand guess blocked by robots.txt, and an msab.no DNS guess fetched as HTTP 200 but produced no owner-proof request and remained ambiguous. Thus this is no search uplift on an unresolved existing candidate/access issue, not evidence the pilot missed correct-company proof. The pilot envelope contains only the search attempt and lacks these prior company-site attempts/snapshots; use final-smoke for this baseline context.

aggregate_diagnosis: No new root bug found. The six Brave calls returned HTTP 200, but two organizations yielded no usable candidates, while Vads? yielded only a third-party customer story and directory entries. No saved page demonstrates correct-company owned-site proof that the unchanged gate rejected. Search results were deliberately not stored, so the two empty candidate lists cannot be diagnosed more finely from this pilot artifact.
request_log_note: Search request receipts intentionally omit URL/query details; no API key or raw Brave response was accessed. Six search requests are identifiable by org, timestamps, and declared cost; 13 additional robots/page requests are recorded.
